time_charter.title: On a time charter the charterer provides and pays for the allowances
lead: Under BIMCO's ETS Allowances Clause for time charter parties (2022) the charterer provides and pays for the allowances for the ship's emissions during the charter and transfers them to the owner, who as the shipping company surrenders them (Directive 2003/87/EC, Article 3gc): on the S4A trip the charterer bears
for the trip, and the owner
for the ballast leg out of the EEA after redelivery.

assumptions: a tonne (DEHSt (German auctions, proxy), monthly average for August 2026) and
dollars per euro (Federal Reserve H.10, August 2026 average), held for every year so that only the phase in moves the cost.

Fuel at the August 2026 common market, each voyage on its Baltic ship's speeds and consumptions: MGO inside emission control areas and at berth in EU ports, VLSFO elsewhere. VLSFO is classed by its ISO 8217 grade (IMO resolution MEPC.391(81)): HFO for RME, RMG and RMK, the default here since most VLSFO is tested against RMG 380, and LFO (3.151 t of CO2 a tonne) for RMA, RMB and RMD.
Methane and nitrous oxide at the warming potentials of the ETS and MRV, 28 and 265 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/1044); FuelEU uses the Renewable Energy Directive's 25 and 298.
A voyage's share of its sourced voyage costs leaves out the port charges at its ports, which have no public figure, so with them the share would be lower.
fueleu: FuelEU Maritime (Regulation (EU) 2023/1805) has applied since 1 January 2025. It sets a limit on the greenhouse gas intensity of the energy a ship uses over a year, 89.34 grams of CO2 equivalent per megajoule from 2025 (2 percent under the 91.16 reference), and a penalty of EUR 2,400 per tonne of VLSFO equivalent energy in deficit. It is settled per ship and year, with banking, borrowing and pooling, so a single voyage has no penalty of its own: the figures below are the penalty the voyage's energy would carry if the ship burnt the same fuel all year, shown beside the TCE and kept out of it.
method: Emissions are the fuel burnt by grade times the factors of the MRV Regulation (EU) 2015/757 as amended: 3.114 t of CO2 per t of HFO, 3.151 for LFO and 3.206 for MGO, with VLSFO classed by its ISO 8217 grade (HFO by default, LFO for RMA to RMD). From 2026 methane and nitrous oxide count, at 0.00005 and 0.00018 g per g of fuel times warming potentials of 28 and 265.

Covered emissions follow Article 3ga of the ETS Directive: 100 percent of a voyage between two EEA ports and of the emissions within a port of call in the EEA, 50 percent of a voyage into or out of the EEA. Allowances are surrendered for 40 percent of 2024 emissions, 70 percent of 2025 and 100 percent from 2026 (Article 3gb); methane and nitrous oxide count from 2026 (Annex I).
